md_description: Workflow for protein crystallography crystallization trials using diverse buffer solutions, capturing the buffer conditions that support protein stability and solubility, measuring crystallization outcomes, and computing derived assessments to optimize conditions for producing higher-quality crystals for structural analysis.

protein_sample.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the purified protein sample itself: identity, source/origin, and core physical-biological descriptors needed to understand what material entered crystallization. I excluded any workflow actions, buffer composition, crystallization setup, imaging, scoring, or optimization details because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Derivative nodes. I also avoided sample/subject/experiment identifiers that would normally be repeated only once at the root, per the no-duplication rule, and I did not repeat any fields already covered by the buffer, crystallization, or imaging nodes.

md_schema.descr: Name of the purified protein used as the starting material for crystallization trials; record the common protein name or construct designation, e.g. 'lysozyme', 'His6-tagged kinase domain'.
Biological source organism of the protein material at the time it was purified; use the organism name, e.g. 'Escherichia coli', 'Homo sapiens'.

Description of the expressed protein construct or variant used for crystallization, including truncations, tags, or mutations if present; measured/recorded once for the starting sample, not during crystallization.

Estimated purity of the protein sample before crystallization trials, expressed as percent (%), typically from SDS-PAGE, SEC, or similar QC near the time of crystallization setup; typical range 0-100.
Concentration of the purified protein stock used to start crystallization trials, in mg/mL; record the concentration measured immediately before drop setup, typically in the range 0.1-100 mg/mL.

Description of the storage or formulation buffer in which the purified protein was maintained before crystallization screening, including major components and approximate conditions if known; this describes the sample's starting environment, not the trial buffers.
Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the purified protein sample was stored prior to crystallization setup, as recorded at sample handling time; typical range -80 to 25.

Approximate molecular mass of the purified protein sample in kilodaltons (kDa), typically from sequence-derived or measured characterization data available before crystallization; typical range 1-1000 kDa.
Known or expected oligomeric state of the purified protein sample at the time of crystallization screening, if characterized; choose the closest categorical description.

buffer_reagent_mix.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how the buffer solutions were prepared: the mixing/formulation protocol, reagent composition, target pH, batch traceability, supplier, catalog number, and any process quality indicator relevant to the preparation step. I excluded intrinsic properties of the resulting trial_buffers entity that belong there, such as final buffer identity as a material sample beyond the preparation process, and I excluded crystallization setup, imaging, and downstream scoring/optimization because those are outside this process’s territory. I also avoided repeating any sample identifiers or experiment identifiers and did not reuse fields already generated for the protein sample node.

md_schema.descr: Names of the reagents or stock components combined to prepare each trial buffer solution, recorded at the preparation step; use standard chemical names, e.g. 'HEPES', 'sodium chloride', 'PEG 3350'.
Concentrations of the reagents used in the buffer formulation at mixing time, in mmol/L (mM); record the target concentration for each named component, typically 0.1-1000 mM.
Target pH of the prepared buffer solution as set during formulation, measured or adjusted during the mixing step before use in crystallization screening; typical range 2-14.
Acid or base used to adjust the buffer pH during preparation, if applicable; record the chemical used for fine adjustment, e.g. 'HCl', 'NaOH'.
Manufacturer or internal batch/lot number of the buffer reagent lot used in preparation, recorded at formulation time for traceability; use the supplier's lot identifier format, e.g. 'L12345'.
Supplier or manufacturer name for the reagent or stock component used in the buffer preparation, recorded at the time of solution formulation; e.g. 'Sigma-Aldrich', 'Thermo Fisher'.
Supplier catalog number for the reagent or buffer component used in the preparation step, recorded for traceability; use the vendor part number format, e.g. 'H0267'.

Brief description of the preparation procedure used to combine and adjust the buffer reagents, including dissolution order, dilution steps, and any sterilization or filtration applied during formulation.
Indicator of whether the buffer formulation step produced a usable trial buffer meeting the planned composition and pH before crystallization setup.

trial_buffers.reasoning: I removed the colliding fields buffer_batch_number, buffer_supplier_name, and buffer_catalog_number because they were already generated in earlier DAG steps and cannot be repeated under the no-duplication rule. I kept only entity-level attributes that uniquely describe the prepared trial buffer material itself, such as its identity, composition, pH, concentration, and storage/handling conditions. I excluded preparation procedure details because those belong to the upstream buffer_reagent_mix process, and I excluded crystallization/imaging/scoring fields because those belong to downstream nodes.

md_schema.descr: Name or label assigned to each prepared trial buffer solution used in crystallization screening, e.g. 'Buffer A', 'HEPES 0.1 M pH 7.5'; record the name used to identify the buffer entity.

Human-readable description of the final buffer composition as prepared, including major components and their concentrations if known; this describes the buffer entity itself, not the mixing procedure.
Measured or specified pH of the prepared buffer solution at the time it is used for crystallization screening; typical range 2-14.
Overall concentration of the main buffer species or relevant solute concentration in mmol/L (mM) for the prepared trial buffer, measured or recorded for the entity; typical range 0.1-1000 mM.
Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the prepared trial buffer was stored before use in crystallization, if tracked; typical range -80 to 25.
Qualitative storage condition of the prepared trial buffer prior to crystallization use, such as 'refrigerated', 'frozen', or 'room_temperature'.

setup_crystallization_drops.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the setup parameters describing how protein sample and trial buffers were combined to create crystallization drops: drop composition, mixing ratios/volumes, crystallization method, plate format, incubation setup, and a basic setup success/quality indicator. I excluded intrinsic properties of the protein sample and trial buffers because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded imaging, raw signal properties, and downstream crystal quality/optimization outputs because those belong to Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes. I also avoided fields that collide with previously generated buffer traceability fields, including batch, supplier, and catalog number, and did not repeat any sample identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Crystallization drop setup method used to combine the protein sample with trial buffer solutions, recorded at the time of screening; examples include 'sitting drop vapor diffusion', 'hanging drop vapor diffusion', or 'microbatch'.
Volume ratio of protein solution to trial buffer solution used when preparing each crystallization drop, recorded during setup; typical values are expressed as ratios such as 1:1, 2:1, or 1:2.
Total volume of the crystallization drop prepared for screening, in microliters (µL), measured at setup time; typical range 0.1-20 µL.
Volume of protein solution added to each crystallization drop, in microliters (µL), recorded during setup; typical range 0.01-20 µL.
Volume of trial buffer solution added to each crystallization drop, in microliters (µL), recorded during setup; typical range 0.01-20 µL.
Type of plate, tray, or vessel used to set up the crystallization drops, recorded at the setup step; e.g. '96-well sitting drop plate', '24-well plate'.
Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the crystallization drops were placed immediately after setup for screening; typical range 0-30.
Number of replicate crystallization drops prepared for the same protein-buffer condition at setup time; typical range 1-100.
Indicator of whether the crystallization drop array was successfully prepared and placed into incubation without setup failure.

crystallization_drops.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the physical crystallization drop array after setup: its container identity, condition indexing, physical dimensions/appearance, incubation state, and whether visible precipitate or phase separation is present. I excluded how the drops were assembled because that belongs to the upstream process, and I excluded imaging, file-level raw data, and quality scoring because those belong to Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any previously generated sample or buffer traceability fields and did not include the setup ratios or volumes already covered by the crystallization setup process.

md_schema.descr: Name or label for the crystallization drop array or trial plate region, used to identify the physical set of drops being observed; e.g. 'screen 1 plate A'.
Total number of individual crystallization drops or wells in the array being tracked as an entity, counted after setup and before imaging; typical range 1-10000.

Index or position code linking each crystallization drop to its protein-buffer condition within the array, recorded as the physical trial identifier for later imaging and scoring; use the lab's well or spot notation, e.g. 'A01', 'B12'.
Observed or nominal volume of an individual crystallization drop, in microliters (µL), as a property of the physical drop after setup; typical range 0.1-20 µL.
Qualitative visual state of the crystallization drop at the time of observation, describing gross appearance before detailed imaging analysis.
Elapsed time in hours since drop setup when the crystallization drop was inspected or recorded as an entity state; typical range 0-10000 hours.
Temperature in degrees Celsius of the environment where the crystallization drops are physically held during observation, if tracked as a property of the entity state; typical range 0-30.
Whether a reservoir or cover solution is present in the crystallization setup surrounding the drop, as a physical property of the trial arrangement.

capture_crystal_images.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration for imaging the crystallization drops: microscope/camera identity, objective and illumination settings, imaging mode, acquisition timing, and capture-level focus/exposure settings. I excluded sample properties, drop composition, and file-level raw image attributes because those belong to the entity/signal nodes, and I excluded image analysis or crystal scoring because those belong to downstream process/derivative nodes. I also avoided any fields already generated for the protein sample, buffer preparation, trial buffers, or crystallization drop setup, and I kept manufacturer/model/serial information on the capture instrument as required.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the automated imaging system or microscope used to capture crystallization drop images, recorded for the capture session; e.g. 'Molecular Devices', 'Hamamatsu'.
Model name or number of the imaging instrument used for crystallization drop capture, recorded at the session level; e.g. 'ImageXpress Micro 4'.
Serial number of the imaging instrument used for the capture session, recorded for traceability; use the instrument serial identifier format as labeled on the device.
Objective magnification used during crystal image capture, recorded as the active microscope setting at the time of imaging; typical values include 1x, 2x, 4x, 10x, 20x, 40x.
Illumination mode used for imaging the crystallization drops, recorded at capture time; choose the acquisition illumination path or contrast method used for the session.
Camera exposure time in milliseconds used during image acquisition, recorded for the capture session; typical range 0.01-10000 ms.
Spatial image resolution produced by the imaging system, recorded as pixel dimensions of the acquired frame at capture time, e.g. 2048x2048.
Focus offset applied relative to the nominal focal plane during crystal image capture, in micrometers (µm); recorded as a capture setting, typical range -500 to 500 µm.
Elapsed time in hours from drop setup to the imaging session, recorded when images were captured; typical range 0-10000 hours.

raw_crystallization_images.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw file- and artefact-level properties of the microscopy images: file format, size, pixel dimensions, channel count, bit depth, storage location, and technical quality indicators. I excluded microscope settings and imaging session details because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded crystal presence/quality interpretation because that belongs to downstream Process and Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any fields already generated for the sample, buffers, drop setup, or capture session.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw microscopy image file representing a crystallization drop, recorded as the stored artefact identifier; e.g. 'plateA_A01_t1.tif'.
File format of the raw crystallization image data, recorded at the signal level; e.g. 'tif', 'png', 'nd2', 'czi'.
Size of the raw image file in bytes, measured from the stored artefact after acquisition; typical range 1e3-1e12 bytes.
Horizontal pixel dimension of the raw crystallization image, recorded from the file metadata; typical range 1-100000 px.
Vertical pixel dimension of the raw crystallization image, recorded from the file metadata; typical range 1-100000 px.
Number of image channels present in the raw microscopy file, recorded from the file metadata; typical range 1-100.
Bit depth of the raw image data, recorded from the file metadata as an integer number of bits per pixel per channel; typical values include 8, 12, 16, or 32.
File path, URI, or other storage location where the raw crystallization image is stored, recorded for data access and reuse; e.g. 's3://bucket/path/file.tif' or '/data/run1/file.tif'.
Technical quality flag describing whether the raw image file is usable for downstream analysis, based on file integrity and acquisition completeness rather than crystal interpretation.

crystal_quality_scoring.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only how the image analysis was performed and the key parameters or outputs of the scoring procedure: analysis algorithm, software settings, scoring rubric, and a process-level success/quality indicator. I excluded capture settings and raw image file properties because those belong to upstream Capture and Signal nodes, and I excluded the computed score values themselves where they are better represented on the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided any fields already generated for the protein sample, buffer preparation, trial buffers, or crystallization setup, and I kept software name/version/repository on the process node as required.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analysis package used to evaluate crystallization images, recorded at the scoring step; e.g. 'CellProfiler', 'Python script', 'CrystalScore'.
Version of the analysis software used for crystal quality scoring, recorded at the time of processing; e.g. '3.1.9'.
Repository, package source, or code location for the analysis software used in scoring, recorded for reproducibility; e.g. URL, Git commit, or package name.
Algorithm or analysis method used to detect or score crystals in the images, recorded at processing time; e.g. 'thresholding', 'CNN classifier', 'rule-based morphology scorer'.

Decision threshold used by the scoring method to classify crystal presence or quality, recorded during analysis; units depend on the algorithm and should be noted in the description if applicable, typical range 0-1 or score units.
Primary metric used to summarize image-based crystallization outcome, recorded at the scoring step; e.g. 'crystal_presence', 'largest_crystal_size', 'morphology_score'.
Brief description of the analysis workflow used to score crystallization images, including preprocessing, feature extraction, and classification steps applied to the raw images.
Indicator of whether the image analysis and scoring process completed successfully for the analyzed images without processing failure.

crystal_quality_scores.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed result fields that summarize the crystallization outcome: score values, hit classification, morphology/size summary, and output-level quality indicators. I excluded the raw image properties and capture settings because those belong to upstream Signal and Capture nodes, and I excluded the analysis algorithm/software settings because those belong to the upstream scoring Process node. I also avoided repeating any fields already generated for the protein sample, buffers, trial setup, or image analysis process, and I did not use any identifiers that would collide with prior DAG steps.

md_schema.descr: Computed score representing whether crystals were detected in the analyzed crystallization image or condition, produced by the crystal quality scoring step; score scale should be consistent within the dataset, commonly 0-1 or 0-100.

Computed metric summarizing crystal size in the analyzed condition, produced from image analysis; units and scale depend on the scoring method, commonly normalized score or micrometers if directly estimated.

Computed metric summarizing crystal morphology or shape quality from the analyzed images, produced by the scoring workflow; higher values should indicate more favorable morphology according to the dataset convention.
Derived classification of the crystallization outcome for a condition, assigned from the computed analysis results.
Short textual summary of the computed crystallization outcome for the condition, such as 'small single crystals observed' or 'no crystals, heavy precipitate'; generated from the scored results.
Confidence or certainty associated with the computed crystal quality result, as produced by the analysis workflow; typical range 0-1 or 0-100 depending on the scoring convention.
Indicator that the computed crystal quality result passed internal validity checks and is suitable for downstream optimization.

condition_optimization.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the optimization procedure and its key settings for integrating crystal quality metrics with buffer-condition annotations: the optimization method, objective/selection criteria, ranking or scoring rule, and process-level success indicator. I excluded the raw crystal quality scores themselves because those belong to the upstream Derivative node, and I excluded the detailed buffer composition/pH values because those belong to the upstream trial_buffers Entity node. I also excluded any output table properties such as final recommended conditions, since those belong to the downstream optimized_crystallization_conditions Derivative node. I avoided repeating already generated field names and did not reuse buffer batch/supplier/catalog identifiers that were previously flagged as collisions.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software, script, or analysis package used to optimize crystallization conditions, recorded at the processing step; e.g. 'scikit-learn', 'R script', 'Optuna pipeline'.
Version of the optimization software or pipeline used to integrate crystal quality metrics with buffer annotations, recorded for reproducibility; e.g. '1.2.0'.
Repository, package source, or code location for the optimization software used in this process, recorded for traceability; e.g. URL or Git commit hash.
Name of the optimization or ranking method used to identify favorable buffer conditions, recorded during analysis; e.g. 'Bayesian optimization', 'rule-based ranking', 'multi-criteria scoring'.
Description of the objective used to rank buffer conditions, such as maximizing crystal presence, size, morphology, or a weighted composite of these metrics.
Primary criterion used to select preferred crystallization conditions from the integrated analysis, recorded at the process stage; e.g. 'highest hit rate', 'best composite score', 'largest crystals'.
Number of buffer conditions or trials evaluated by the optimization procedure, counted at the processing step; typical range 1-100000.
Indicator of whether the optimization process completed successfully and produced a usable ranking or selection of buffer conditions.

optimized_crystallization_conditions.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only the computed optimized result fields: the selected buffer condition identity, recommended composition/pH, ranking or score, and a derived quality summary describing why the condition is favorable. I excluded upstream buffer formulation details because those belong to the trial_buffers entity and condition_optimization process, and I excluded raw crystal scores and optimization software settings because those belong to the upstream derivative/process nodes. I also avoided field-name collisions with already generated fields, especially the buffer traceability identifiers that were previously flagged as duplicates, and I kept the output focused on the reusable optimization result table.

md_schema.descr: Label or identifier for the recommended crystallization condition in the optimized result table, used to reference the selected buffer condition; e.g. 'Condition 12', 'best_hit_03'.

Computed recommended buffer composition for the optimized crystallization condition, summarized from the selected trial results; this is the derived recommendation, not the original preparation record.
Recommended pH of the optimized buffer condition, derived from the condition ranking/selection step; typical range 2-14.
Rank of the buffer condition in the optimized list, where 1 indicates the most favorable condition according to the chosen objective.
Derived score assigned to the recommended buffer condition by the optimization procedure; the scale should match the dataset convention, commonly 0-1 or 0-100.
Short textual summary of why the buffer condition was selected, such as 'best crystal morphology and highest hit rate' or 'improved solubility and clear drops'.
Indicator that the optimized condition is considered suitable for follow-up crystal growth and structural analysis based on the derived ranking and quality criteria.
Indicator that the optimized condition result passed checks and is usable as the final derived output of the workflow.
